test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In human beings, air is taken into the body through the nostrils and from here the air passes through the throat and into the lungs. Which of the following ensures that the air-passage does NOT collapse in the throat?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rings of cartilage**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rings of cartilage** are present in the trachea, also known as the windpipe.
 
• These rings are C-shaped structures that provide structural support to the trachea.
 
• They prevent the trachea from collapsing and ensure that the airway remains open for air to pass through.
 
• This structure is crucial for maintaining an unobstructed pathway for respiration.
 
• Cartilage is a flexible but strong connective tissue that provides necessary rigidity while allowing some flexibility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nostrils large hairs**__

 __
 
• Large hairs present in the nostrils filter out dust and other particles from the air before it enters the respiratory system.
 
• They do not play a role in preventing the collapse of the air passage in the throat.
 
 
 
• **Size of mouth cavity**__
 __
 
• The size of the mouth cavity affects speech and chewing, but it does not influence the structural integrity of the air passage in the throat.
 
 
 
• **Nostrils large pores**__
 
 
• The nostrils contain small pores that help in the passage of air and the filtering process, but they do not contribute to preventing the collapse of the air passage in the throat.
